BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. # Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Preliminary note on the Seller's preamble.** The covering note asserts that the positions are "market standard", "settled at principal level by both deal teams", "agreed" and "FINAL". Per playbook sec 0.4/6.3, none of that is accepted. We have no record of principal-level agreement, no Amelia Frost written authority for any fallback, and the Seller's own Disclosure Letter (para 11) expressly disclaims any "negotiation position or approval". Treat the draft as an opening position.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap (cl 12.1)**
- *Seller:* 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- *Buyer wants:* 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** The 20% figure matching our conditional fallback does not clear it – it is usable only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft, and none exists.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket (cl 12.2)**
- *Seller:* de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only (deductible) recovery.
- *Buyer wants:* de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; tipping basket (first-dollar recovery once exceeded).
- *Recommendation:* **Reject all three elements.** The Seller's thresholds are 5x our positions and the deductible structure converts the basket into a permanent AUD 250,000 loss for the buyer.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit (cl 12.3/13)**
- *Seller:* 18 months; plus a sweep that any limitation applies to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise".
- *Buyer wants:* 24 months for general claims; limitations apply only to the category they are drafted for.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject; counter at 24 months and delete the all-Claims sweep.** 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost written approval (none given), and the sweep would silently pull Title, Tax, IP, indemnity and covenant claims under the general regime.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- *Seller:* capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- *Buyer wants:* separate regime – 100% of price cap, at least six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject outright.** Title to the shares is the entire consideration; capping it at 20% and 18 months would leave the buyer unprotected on the core asset.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)**
- *Seller:* limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature" – no fraud carve-out.
- *Buyer wants:* fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject; insert express carve-out.** This is a non-waivable playbook item and the Seller's drafting purports to limit liability for its own fraud.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope (Sch 7; Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2)**
- *Seller:* whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012 as at 22 Sept 2026), Accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable records all deemed disclosed.
- *Buyer wants:* only specific, fair disclosure with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no general data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject paras 1.1–1.2; require specific disclosures only.** General disclosure would qualify every warranty by reference to the entire record and gut the warranty package.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)**
- *Seller:* no claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records".
- *Buyer wants:* delete the blanket exclusion; any knowledge qualifier limited to named seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry, and never applying to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- *Recommendation:* **Delete cl 8.3.** "Discoverable" imputes constructive knowledge of the whole data room and public records, which effectively re-imports general disclosure through the back door.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3)**
- *Seller:* reasonable endeavours only; consent deemed satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. Disclosure Letter para 2 confirms no final consent and no evidence of cl 11.3 conditions being met.
- *Buyer wants:* an effective consent as a Condition Precedent, plus evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, delivered before Completion.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject; make effective consent plus condition-satisfaction evidence a hard CP.** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue, so "consent-on-delivery" and reasonable endeavours are inadequate for a material customer.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (cl 2/7)**
- *Seller:* ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion". Disclosure Letter para 3 confirms not repaid and no discharge in the data room.
- *Buyer wants:* current payout figure, repayment directly from Completion funds, and effective security releases delivered at Completion (post-completion release only with an irrevocable bank undertaking and Amelia Frost approval).
- *Recommendation:* **Reject post-completion release; require payout letter, direct repayment and releases at Completion.** The buyer would otherwise acquire a company encumbered by AUD 3.2m of debt in a supposedly debt-free deal, with change-of-control (cl 8.1) exposure.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (Funds flow; DD-005)**
- *Seller:* AUD 420,000 closing bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. Disclosure Letter para 5 confirms omission and is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- *Buyer wants:* AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item deducted from the price, or expressly seller-funded with an indemnity.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject; require explicit line item or seller-funded indemnity.** A bonus triggered by Completion is a transaction cost of the Seller, and silence in the funds flow would leave the buyer paying it post-Completion.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1)**
- *Seller:* indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate". Disclosure Letter para 4: AUD 180,000 recorded open in DD-010 (not bank-verified either way); no receipt or confirmatory assignment on file.
- *Buyer wants:* a broadened indemnity covering all loss arising from non-transfer or defective ownership of SOW3 Project Materials (including third-party claims and remediation), while preserving the cure of paying the SOW3 fees and obtaining a confirmatory assignment pre-Completion.
- *Recommendation:* **Broaden the indemnity and require payment evidence plus confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable.** Under DD-004 cl 7.3 title to the IP does not pass until every fee is cleared, so a payment-only indemnity does not cover the real risk – loss of the IP itself.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6; DD-006)**
- *Seller:* "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material. Disclosure Letter para 6: ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address; access, scope and notification duty all undetermined.
- *Buyer wants:* covenant to preserve logs, complete the investigation, provide updates through to Completion, and a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric claim either way.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject the "not material" characterisation; insert investigation/update covenants and a specific indemnity, no price adjustment at this stage.** The facts are unresolved and the Seller's own letter declines to characterise them, so the buyer should neither accept "immaterial" nor assert a breach.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008/DD-011)**
- *Seller:* three renewals of AUD 110,000 (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure Letter para 8 does not state whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- *Buyer wants:* a DD assessment of timing, scope and terminability before accepting any characterisation; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- *Recommendation:* **Hold position – do not accept "ordinary course" and do not claim a deduction; request renewal terms and accrual status.** The Seller's own disclosure does not support its characterisation, and the playbook does not pre-judge the answer.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation (cl 12.3 sweep; Tax/IP note)**
- *Seller:* all limitations apply to all Claims unless stated otherwise; Tax and IP treated as "settled under the general regime".
- *Buyer wants:* Title, Tax, IP, payment (price/leakage) and covenant claims as separate categories with their own caps, periods and thresholds; no hidden general-regime override.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject; redraft cl 12/13 with express category schedules.** The "unless expressly stated otherwise" default is a hidden override that would collapse every bespoke regime into 20% / 18 months.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification (DD-012)**
- *Seller:* title to 100% evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012. Disclosure Letter para 10 concedes this is the source relied on and that buyer verification is incomplete.
- *Buyer wants:* independent evidence – ASIC extracts, PPSR searches, board/shareholder authorisations, certified register and encumbrance confirmations – plus Riverlark releases (see N-009).
- *Recommendation:* **Do not accept DD-012 as proof; commission independent title, encumbrance and authority searches before signing.** A company-maintained register supplied by the Seller is an internal source, not independent verification.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- *Seller:* "settled under the general regime".
- *Buyer wants:* Tax and IP terms expressly remain OPEN pending agreement of separate regimes (noting the playbook assumes no unlimited liability and no resolution yet).
- *Recommendation:* **Reject "settled"; record Tax and IP as open items in the issues list.** Nothing has been agreed, and folding them into the general regime would pre-empt the separate-category negotiation under N-014.

---

**Summary for the deal team:** every substantive Seller position departs from the playbook; none should be accepted on the basis of the "agreed/FINAL/market" assertions. Items requiring escalation to Amelia Frost only if we later wish to move: N-001 (20% cap), N-003 (18 months), N-009 (any post-completion release). Immediate action items: independent title searches (N-015), Riverlark payout letter (N-009), Bluefen consent and cl 11.3 evidence (N-008), Ironquay payment evidence and assignment (N-011), DD-006 investigation updates (N-012), Sandbar renewal terms (N-013).
